shorts.description:
Something that’s helped me post more:

Instead of: “How will my audience take this?’

I ask: “Would I post it anyways?”

And if so, I go for it. And your brand will adjust to reality. Which is endlessly more sustainable than an algorithm driven version of yourself you’ll never be
shorts.title: Good Content Beats Production Every Time

shorts.description:
A lot of management just comes down to:

Tell them what you want
Show them how to do it
Check in to make sure they did
Give feedback on the outcome

And just doing that until you die.
shorts.title: You're Asking Them to Guess and Somehow Get It Right

shorts.description:
Find what works. 
Do more of what works.
Find the thing preventing you from doing more of what works. 
Solve it.
Do more of what works.
Repeat.
shorts.title: Stop Judging Yourself for What's Actually Working

shorts.description:
If you've been thinking about starting a business for more than 6 months, stop.

Just offer to do something. Anything. For someone else. In exchange for money. Today.

And when you do, congrats, you own a business. 

Now you just gotta do more and better until the day you die.
shorts.title: You're Running 6 Businesses and That's Your Problem

shorts.description: Feeling like everything sucks, totally uncertain of the future, wishing you had known what you know now, while still being underwater with work is just a normal part of entrepreneurship.
shorts.title: Reframe Your Reality as Someone Else's Dream

shorts.description: You can beat 99% of people without being smarter or luckier, but by being willing to endure pain and uncertainty for longer.
shorts.title: Winners and Losers Have the Same Goals

shorts.description:
There are a million ways to make a million dollars. 

It doesn’t matter which one you pick. 

It just matters that you pick.
shorts.title: Every Business Can Hit $100K/Month Profit

shorts.description:
Figure out what you want. 
Ignore the opinions of others. 
Do so much work it would be unreasonable that you fail.
Realize it never mattered to begin with.
Help others once you get there.
shorts.title: By the Time You Achieve Your Goal, It Already Feels Small

shorts.description:
One of the hardest business lessons I’ve had to learn is: you don’t try to get bigger.

Instead, you try and get better. 

The better you get, the bigger your customers will demand you become. 

Quality creates demand. 
Demand creates growth.

Not the other way around.
shorts.title: Your Business Isn't Failing Because of the Market

shorts.description:
If you're split between two paths, pick the one with the better story.
At the end of your life, it's all your gonna have left anyways.
shorts.title: Stop Deciding and You Lose Both

shorts.description:
Easy model for business growth:

Give first. 
Don’t trade. 
Give. 
To lots of people. 
For free. 
Without asking for anything.
Keep going until someone wants more. Then you’re good enough to charge. 
Until then. 
Keep giving and getting better.
shorts.title: You Probably Suck, Which Is Why You Shouldn't Charge Yet

shorts.description:
The bigger the monster, the greater the hero. 

Whatever trials you’re going through, just remember they will be the stories you tell. 

…And no one likes a boring success story.
shorts.title: The Fear Only Goes Away When You Do the Thing

shorts.description: If you tell people you’re 10 years older than you really are, you get amazing compliments about how young you look. 😂
shorts.title: I Pretended My Boss Existed to Close Deals at 22

shorts.description: A lot of making a plan work comes down to sticking with the plan you originally started with without thinking things have changed when all they did was get hard.
shorts.title: The Fact That You're Uncomfortable Is Why You Should Persist

shorts.description:
My super productive day formula:

1) Remove all apps (this is the hardest & most effective - social, slack, phone call, sms, I mean everything)
2) Cover windows/visual distractions 
3) Wear ear plugs + ear muffs
4) Remove meetings
5) Stimulate (caffeine, nicotine, + your faves)
6) Set a timer per task
7) Rack em & stack em

Once you remove everything, all that’s left is the work.

And the best part is: removing stuff is free.
shorts.title: You Don't Lack Focus, You're Focusing on the Wrong Things

shorts.description:
People want to find their passion. 
But you don’t find it, you create it. 
And you create by getting good at something. 
And to get good at stuff, you start by doing something you suck at.
Then, you get good.
Then, you like it.
Then, people ask you how you found your passion.

Answer: By starting when you sucked and not giving up.
shorts.title: Greatness Rejects All First Time Applicants

shorts.description:
The best offer to sell for growth:

If you get 10 new clients/mo at $2,500/mo, and don’t lose them. In 5 years, you have a $1.5M/mo business with good margins.

Best way to grow is - fix the product so you don’t lose all your clients every year.

Then, growth becomes inevitable.
shorts.title: How to Sell a $1.5M Business for $500K

shorts.description:
The “sweet spot” for companies to go public is 5-7 years after they are founded. 

Why this matters…

No matter how old or young you are, you’re only 5-7 years away from accomplishing anything.

Never too late to think big.
shorts.title: By Saying It's Too Late, You're Accepting You'll Accomplish Nothing

shorts.description:
A big entrepreneurial mistake I see is reaching a new problem you don’t know how to solve then assuming you need to change your business.

When in reality, you just need to confront the problem and realize that each big problem you solve separates you further from the pack.
shorts.title: Are You Solving a Problem That Hasn't Happened Yet?

shorts.description:
Decisions only you can make for yourself:

Who you love
What’s work is worth your time
Where you call home
What “enough” means for you
How much risk to take
When to walk away

If someone doesn’t have a stake in the outcome they shouldn’t have a say in the decision.
shorts.title: What Conditions Need to Be True Before You Take the Risk?

shorts.description:
The bigger the monster, the greater the hero. 

Whatever trials you’re going through, just remember they will be the stories you tell. 

…And no one likes a boring success story.
shorts.title: The Fear Only Goes Away When You Do the Thing

shorts.description:
The reason you want to do the new thing is because you don’t know how to keep growing the old thing. 

Fix the problem don’t start a new business.
shorts.title: You're Blaming the Market for a Business Problem

shorts.description:
Everyone’s childhood was difficult. 
Get over it. 

And if you want to win the award for hardest childhood - congrats. You win. 

Feel better? 

Right. 

No one cares about what happened to you then. 

Only what you can make happen now.
shorts.title: Your Sob Story Doesn't Change Your Condition

shorts.description:
People say “do or die” like it’s a choice.
Reality is you’re going to die either way. 
So you might as well do something cool before you do.
And if you don’t, the only person who loses out is you.
shorts.title: You're Not Losing by Choosing, You're Losing by Not Deciding

shorts.description:
Easy model for business growth:

Give first. 
Don’t trade. 
Give. 
To lots of people. 
For free. 
Without asking for anything.
Keep going until someone wants more. Then you’re good enough to charge. 
Until then. 
Keep giving and getting better.
shorts.title: You Probably Suck, So Don't Charge Yet

shorts.description:
Most entrepreneurs can dramatically increase their net worth by doing less.

If you can hire the people to run your business without you, truly, as in, someone else could buy the bank account and it would continue to get deposits…you have a valuable thing. 

Worth prioritizing.
shorts.title: There's a $10M Version of You Who Doesn't Hesitate

shorts.description: If you tell people you’re 10 years older than you really are, you get amazing compliments about how young you look. 😂
shorts.title: Pretend You're Not the Owner

shorts.description: A lot of making a plan work comes down to sticking with the plan you originally started with without thinking things have changed when all they did was get hard.
shorts.title: How You Feel and What You Do Don't Need to Correlate

shorts.description:
Figure out what you want. 
Ignore the opinions of others. 
Do so much work it would be unreasonable that you fail.
Realize it never mattered to begin with.
Help others once you get there.
shorts.title: By the Time You Win, the Goal Already Feels Small

shorts.description:
How many businesses does it take to make a millionaire?

One. 

Is it easier to do two things or one? 

One.

How many businesses do people have to become billionaires?

One.

And yet…

Everyone is fooled by people saying to have 7 income streams who don’t even have one.

Focus.
shorts.title: You Cannot Run Two Businesses Well

shorts.description:
The importance of betting big:

In entrepreneurship, you will lose more times than you win. So you just need to make sure that when you win, you win so big, it overshadows all your losses.

No one cares about small victories or defeats.
shorts.title: You've Become Successful Enough That You Must Raise Your Stakes

shorts.description:
Anyone can sell stuff to people to make some money.

To make lots of money you either need to sell lots of people or get the people you sold to sell lots people for you (because of how good your stuff was).

The former is easier in the beginning. The ladder is easier in the end.
shorts.title: You're Not Trapped, You're Just Lying to Yourself

shorts.description: If you’re good at business, you make more money doing the opportunity than selling it.
shorts.title: The Fastest Money You Make Is Selling Shovels

shorts.description:
You don’t become confident by shouting affirmations in the mirror, but by having a stack of undeniable proof that you are who you say you are.

Outwork your self doubt.
shorts.title: Give Yourself Undeniable Proof You Are Who You Say You Are

shorts.description:
What's funny about taking life risk rather than financial risk is that if it doesn't go well, you're literally back in the same position that you started, except smarter.

When u think about it like that, you want to cash in as many life lotto tickets as you can, not as few.
shorts.title: You're 19 With $700K — Bet Big on Yourself

shorts.description: It’s better to find what people say yes to then work backwards to profit than get no one to say yes with a hypothetical margin.
shorts.title: How I'd Take a $27M Law Firm National

shorts.description:
Most entrepreneurial companies struggle not because of starvation (lack of opportunity) but because of choking to death (taking on too many opportunities at once). 

“If everything is important, nothing is.”
shorts.title: Businesses Die From Indigestion, Not Starvation

shorts.description:
I’m gonna say this without trying to insult anyone…

I get asked how I come up with all the content across: YT, TT, Twitter, LI, IG, FB, Pod, Books, etc.

If you spend your time doing the stuff, you don’t need to come up with anything. Just talk about what you did.
shorts.title: Talk About the Shit You Do and They'll Pay You to Do It

shorts.description:
Amateur: “I’m starting a bunch of different businesses to see which one works!”

Veteran: “I’m spending every waking hour on this one detail of my product to delight customers.”

Focus…or get beat by someone who does.
shorts.title: Your Downside Protection is Costing You 2 Years of Growth

shorts.description:
Download your free scaling roadmap here: https://www.acquisition.com/roadmap-yt-d

If you’re new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I’m the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It’s a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I’ll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Opened 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything. 
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time. 
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked. 
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.  
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months. 
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal. 
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com, which is a platform for people to build communities online, making a living doing what they love, with people like them.
36 yrs old: I did a $106M book launch selling 3.6M copies of my $100M Money Models book, in 72 hours, breaking the Guinness world record for the fastest selling non-fiction book of all time.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we’re all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win. 

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex

DISCLOSURE 
Information shared here is for educational purposes only.  Individuals and business owners should evaluate their own business strategies, and identify any potential risks.  The information shared here is not a guarantee of success. Your results may vary.
Copyright © 2026.

shorts.description: If an employee never provides a solution, they are the problem.
shorts.title: Are They Offering Solutions or Problems to Your Solutions?

shorts.description:
The first time you buy something takes lots of thought.

Reordering, takes very little.

Both transactions make the company the same amount of money.

Which kind of business do you want to build…a first time sales business or a reorder business?

Right…then act like it.
shorts.title: How to Scale a Low-Ticket Consumer Brand

shorts.description: Building a $1,000,000 Business for a Stranger in 56 Mins
shorts.title: How to Turn a $4.97 Product Into $1,000,000

shorts.description:
Who you sell to matters as much (or more than) the value you provide:

If you help a billionaire lose weight you can charge 100x more than gen pop. 

Because in a very real way, that more narrowly defined market values the solution at a higher dollar amount.
shorts.title: You're Not Selling Videos, You're Selling a Result
